a negation of a NEGATION. `!!x` and `x` are the same truth and DIFFERENT TREES, so collapsing it would hand back a formula the member did not write, and rendering it would need a control the picker does not have — one toggle per condition says WHETHER it is negated, not how many times. a crossing is a CONDITION with a row of its own, never a TERM inside a comparison — the term slots offer the table's term-valued functions and nothing else. (`crossOver(close, open)` itself is now a row: see the crossing block in criteria.test.js.)
a nested call inside a crossing operand — a crossing row's sides are picker TERMS and the picker shows one level, exactly as a comparison row does

a negated EXPRESSION is arithmetic, and arithmetic terms are still refused. A negative LITERAL is now a number the picker shows (`pct_vs_ema20 >= -2`), and this is the line between the two: the operand must be a literal.

a negative literal inside a CALL puts an operator node in an argument slot, and a function's `int` argument is a LOOKBACK. Refused on BOTH sides — `readTerm` here, `leafSource` when spelling — so the two directions cannot disagree.

a bars-ago qualifier on a GROUP. A one-child group spells its child and nothing else, so a qualified group and a qualified leaf would be two pickers with ONE tree — the round trip would stop being an identity. The qualifier rides the leaf it reads. (`(close > open)[1]` itself is now a row: see the qualifier block in criteria.test.js.)

a bars-ago qualifier OUTSIDE a negation. The picker carries one nesting — the qualifier is the leaf's and the negate toggle is written over the qualified condition, `!(x[1])` — so the other order is refused rather than rendered with a control the row does not have.

a bars-ago qualifier inside a CALL ARGUMENT. A call's arguments are a name picker and a window box; rendering a qualified one would show `sma(close, 20)` for a formula that says something else. Refused on BOTH sides — `readTerm` here, `leafSource` when spelling — exactly as a negative literal in an argument is.
